label: Game B
nuance_found: Score comes from three places: drift (angle and speed, banked with a combo), roadside smashes that chain (a x6 'FLATTENED' chain paid +1,010 and a JACKPOT paid +3,010 once), and near-miss CLIPs on guardrails (+250). A 70 degree drift paid +320. The time of day also ticks and each banked drift is said to bring dawn closer. The real trade-off is clean drifting versus ploughing into roadside objects for chains. I mostly found the smash route by accident and never chained drifts at all.
audio: An ambience loop plus a sequenced synth jingle when scoring, a low engine-like sine, a thump on crashes, and phone vibration on the handbrake. Rain and night changes add atmosphere.
furthest_progress: Yozakura Pass, Easy. Reached in-game 01:47 at night and rain (dawn at 06:00 not reached), 45 mi, score 11,793, combo only ever x1.
control_trouble: Steering with the gas thumb was far too sensitive for my 0.5 s look rate: tiny offsets sent the car into trees, and I could not hold a drift. I count about a quarter of my time as crashed or stuck. A real thumb on a live screen would do much better, but the sharp bends also seem to come up fast.
best_moment: Smashing a roadside cabinet in a x5 chain for a JACKPOT, with the score jumping by about 2,000 in a second and the car sliding on.
worst_moment: Hitting a pole or tree at speed and sitting at 0 mph for 4 s before the magnet rescue, again and again at the same bends.
verdict: It looks like a finished game and it feels great: golden hour fading to night and rain, the car squashing signs, big yellow chain text, the magnet putting me back on the road. I understood driving in seconds but only worked out how scoring really works after about a minute. The crash rescue is nice but it wastes 4 to 5 s each time, and my combo never got above x1 because I could not hold drifts. Smash chains pay far more than clean driving, which feels backwards for a drift game. The potential is there, with drift combos for the expert line. It is more of a 6, and I would try to learn the drift line again.
